photo.question: Should a CV include a photo?
photo.answer: In Uzbekistan many employers expect one, especially state organisations and customer-facing roles. It is a convention, not a legal requirement. If you are applying to an international company or abroad, leave it out — in many countries it is not asked for. The photo is optional here, and leaving it empty costs no space on the page.

language.question: Which language should the CV be in?
language.answer: The language of the job posting. Uzbek for state organisations; Russian is the working language of many private offices in Tashkent; English for international companies and IT. This tool produces all three, and the document language is independent of the site language — you can read the site in Russian and write the CV in Uzbek.

script.question: Latin or Cyrillic script?
script.answer: It depends on who will read it. Younger HR staff and private companies usually expect Latin; older managers and some government offices still find Cyrillic easier. When in doubt, use Latin. One button switches the whole document here, while e-mail, phone and links stay untransliterated.

length.question: How long should a CV be?
length.answer: One page is the right answer for most people. A second page is only justified by substantial experience. A hairline on the sheet shows where the page ends: if your text crosses it, trim the oldest role or tighten the summary.

personal.question: Do I have to give a birth date and marital status?
personal.answer: No. It is a settled local convention in Uzbekistan and many employers expect to see it, but it is not required. Both fields are optional — left blank, those lines do not appear on the finished CV.

fileFormat.question: Should I send a PDF or a Word file?
fileFormat.answer: Sending it to a person directly (e-mail, Telegram) — PDF: it opens exactly as it looks here. Uploading to a job board — .docx: those systems read the file and split it into fields. That is why the .docx here is exported as a single column — automated parsers often scramble a two-column layout.

noExperience.question: I have no work experience. What do I write?
noExperience.answer: Experience is not only formal employment. Internships, coursework projects, volunteering, helping in a family business, freelance jobs — all of it counts. Put education, skills and languages first, and use the summary to say concretely what you have learned and what you can do.

privacy.question: Where is the information I type stored?
privacy.answer: On this device only. The CV is assembled in your browser and never sent to a server. The draft stays in browser storage, so closing the page and coming back keeps your work. The photo is not uploaded anywhere either. No signup is required.
